clue.text: Great Scott! In a novel way he introduced Russian gardening equipment

definitions.text: Great Scott! In a novel way he

parts.note: Ivan is a typical Russian man's name, standing for a Russian
a hoe is a weeding tool

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at a man who brought some Russian garden tools into the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great Scott!' looks like an oath, but it points to Sir Walter Scott, whose novel has this hero; 'introduced' just joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of Sir Walter Scott's historical romance is the knight Wilfred of this name.

clue.text: Live in monastic style

parts.note: a habit is the robe worn by monks and nuns

explanation.surface: A command to live like a monk.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell somewhere is to occupy it as a home.

clue.text: A snobbish get-together in a sound way

parts.note: U means upper-class, the snob's mark of approval
a rally is a mass meeting

explanation.surface: An exclusive party described as sensible or healthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' suggests sensible, but here it means hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the ear and hearing, as opposed to sight.

clue.text: Abode for bingo

explanation.surface: A place to live, given over to a game of numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the call for a full card in bingo is this word, and the game itself is also known by it.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a dwelling; the other is the old name for the numbers game, also the winner's shout.

clue.text: Occult entity that can point to the French in the mind

parts.note: E is East, a point of the compass
le is French for 'the'
mental means of or in the mind

explanation.surface: A spirit able to direct French people inside one's head.
explanation.definitionFit: A spirit of earth, air, fire or water in occult lore is a nature spirit of this kind.

clue.text: First-rate money

explanation.surface: Excellent cash.
explanation.definitionFit: An old exclamation of approval means excellent; the other sense is funds for investment.

clue.text: Third-class pitcher up ended at rail junction…

parts.note: C is the third grade after A and B

indicators.note: upended in a down clue means the jug is turned over, its word read from the bottom up

parts.note: a ewer is a large water jug

explanation.surface: A cheap jug tipped over at a station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up ended' turns EWER into REWE. CREWE is a town in Cheshire, England, famous as a railway junction.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cheshire town long known as one of England's chief railway interchanges.

clue.text: … by earlier actor

parts.note: per means by, as in 'per post'
former means previous

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: the station was reached by a once-famous actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone who acts on stage is an entertainer appearing before an audience.

clue.text: Extinguish the light and call a the guard

explanation.surface: Orders at night: lights off, summon the sentries.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray 'a' in the held text is a misprint. To turn out the guard is the military phrase for calling it out on parade.
explanation.definitionFit: Switching off a lamp and summoning soldiers to parade are both expressed by this phrasal verb.

clue.text: Young skipper joins the rebuilt episcopal palace

parts.note: a lamb is a young sheep that skips about

indicators.note: rebuilt says the letters of the word 'the' are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: A youthful ship's captain joins a team restoring a bishop's residence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skipper' suggests a captain, but here it is a frisking lamb. 'rebuilt' makes ETH from THE. LAMBETH Palace is the Archbishop of Canterbury's London home.
explanation.definitionFit: The London residence of the Archbishop of Canterbury bears this district's name.

clue.text: His true disposition makes him ready for the barber

indicators.note: disposition, in its sense of arrangement, signals the letters set out afresh

explanation.surface: A man's honest nature means he needs a haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposition' looks like temperament but means arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone shaggy and hairy is in need of a trim.

clue.text: A murder reconstructed by listening apparatus

indicators.note: a crime reconstruction suggests the letters being put together again differently

explanation.surface: Police re-enact a killing, aided by bugging equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: The membrane in the ear that vibrates with sound is part of the hearing mechanism.

clue.text: Gazebo for Apollo's gallery

explanation.surface: A summerhouse where a god's art is displayed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Apollo Belvedere is a famous statue named after the Vatican gallery court where it stands.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a raised summerhouse with a view, and also names the Vatican courtyard housing a celebrated Apollo statue.

clue.text: Short weight precedes one refreshing breather

indicators.note: precedes puts the weight before the next word

parts.note: oz is the abbreviation for ounce

explanation.surface: A slight shortfall in weight comes before a refreshing break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breather' suggests a rest; it means something breathed, the bracing sea air of popular belief.
explanation.definitionFit: Seaside air is popularly called by the name of this form of oxygen.

clue.text: Have a 80, good fellow! Make a date!

parts.note: to try is to make an attempt
ST, saint, a good person

explanation.surface: Encouragement to a friend to be brave and ask someone out.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to arrange a lovers' meeting.

clue.text: In the old-fashioned way you are on the beach in tens of hundreds

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, puts the first word on top of the second

parts.note: thou is the archaic form of you
sands are a beach

explanation.surface: Speaking quaintly of people on the shore in their multitudes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ten hundreds make one of these, so many tens of hundreds are a plural of it.

clue.text: Trial marriage as a sporting event

parts.note: a test is a trial
a match is a marriage

explanation.surface: Living together before wedding presented as a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: A TEST MATCH is an international cricket or rugby fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: An international fixture in cricket or rugby is a major sports contest.

clue.text: That's enough! You should refuse oftener

explanation.surface: Advice to someone too willing to agree.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for 'I understand, stop there', and read literally it urges refusing more often.

clue.text: Tattered red woolly becomes Charles II

indicators.note: tattered means torn up, so the letters are pulled apart and rearranged

explanation.surface: A shabby red jumper turns into a king.
explanation.walkthrough: OLD ROWLEY was a nickname of King Charles II, from his favourite racehorse.
explanation.definitionFit: The Restoration monarch was known by this nickname, after a stallion he owned.

clue.text: The shortest dance?

parts.note: a ballroom dance name read as the smallest possible amount of dancing, a single pace

explanation.definitionFit: It is a quick ballroom dance of the early twentieth century, whose name taken literally is a single stride.

clue.text: Comparatively god-like dowser

explanation.surface: A water-finder said to be rather saintly.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both the comparative of a word for godly and a person who finds water with a rod.

clue.text: Sovereign guide for the pen

explanation.surface: A king who directs the writer.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch governs, and a straight-edge guides a pen when drawing lines.

clue.text: A little space for the French stableman?

parts.note: le is French for 'the'
a groom looks after horses

explanation.surface: Asking whether a French stable hand needs some room.
explanation.definitionFit: Space for a seated passenger's knees and feet.

clue.text: Takes up another assumed attitude and lies

explanation.surface: A model shifts position and reclines.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as re-poses, it means strikes a new pose; as one word it means rests or lies down.

clue.text: Mischievous sprites in the chapel vestry

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the words chapel vestry, across the word break

explanation.surface: Naughty spirits lurking where the clergy robe.
explanation.definitionFit: Small pranksome fairy folk of folklore.

clue.text: Getting better by raising the gaze

explanation.surface: Improving by lifting one's eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means improving, of prospects, and literally lifting one's eyes upward.

clue.text: Tilts sideways where they tilt head-on

explanation.surface: Leaning over in the place of jousting.
explanation.walkthrough: To tilt is also to joust, and the jousting ground is called the lists.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship leans to one side, and the enclosed arena for medieval jousting has this plural name.

clue.text: In the beginning help turns up for the sub-continent

indicators.note: the beginning places the little word at the start of the answer
turns up, in a down clue, means the word is read from the bottom upward

parts.note: aid is help

explanation.surface: Assistance first arrives from a large Asian land.
explanation.definitionFit: The country fills most of the South Asian landmass, the subcontinent.

clue.text: The landlord's half-score of little busybodies?

parts.note: a score is twenty, so half is ten
ants are small, ceaselessly busy insects

explanation.surface: A landlord's ten nosy small people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The landlord's' is the definition: the landlord's people, his renters.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who rent property belong, in a sense, to the landlord who lets it.

clue.text: Paradoxically former pupils could be young men

definitions.text: Paradoxically former pupils could be young men

parts.words: Paradoxically former pupils could be young men
parts.note: school leavers are called by a name that pairs aged with lads, which sounds contradictory

explanation.definitionFit: Ex-students of a school are known by a phrase joining aged with lads.

clue.text: Reads by means of customs

parts.note: per means by means of, as in 'per post'
uses are customs or habits

explanation.surface: Studies through customs paperwork.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrutinise a text carefully is to read it.

clue.text: Sums are the making of the backward philosopher

indicators.note: backward tells us the words Sums are are read from right to left

explanation.surface: Arithmetic is what made a slow-witted thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' looks like it describes a dim philosopher; it is the reversal sign.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch Renaissance humanist scholar is ranked among the great thinkers.
